questions.question: Explain the difference between exports and imports, and give examples for South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Exports are goods sold to other countries, which bring money into the country. South Africa exports minerals such as platinum, gold, coal and iron ore, as well as citrus fruit, wine and cars. Imports are goods bought from other countries, such as crude oil and fuel, machines, phones and medicines.

questions.question: Use cocoa or gold to explain how value is added to a raw material, and why this matters for fair trade.
questions.expected_answer: Cocoa beans are grown on small farms in West Africa, fermented and dried, then roasted and ground in factories and mixed with sugar and milk to make chocolate. Each stage of work adds value, so the chocolate is worth much more than the beans. Because the farmers usually get only a small share of the final price, fair trade tries to give them a fair minimum price and a premium for community projects.

questions.question: Give three reasons why Europeans explored, and describe how the sea route to the East was found.
questions.expected_answer: Europeans explored out of curiosity, for trade and profit from spices and silk, to spread Christianity and to find a sea route to the East. New tools such as the compass, the astrolabe and the caravel helped them. In 1488, Bartolomeu Dias was the first European to sail around the southern tip of Africa, and in 1497 to 1498, Vasco da Gama sailed around the Cape and, with a pilot from Malindi, reached Calicut in India.
